subject: Audit rights / evidence cadence + pen-test scope — MSA & Order Form coordination
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@atlashealth.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: 2027-04-03T08:05:00-04:00
Subject: Audit rights / evidence cadence and pen-test window

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to confirm a couple items so we can finalize the Order Form and move to signatures:

- Can you confirm the exact audit rights we include in the security exhibit? Our legal team prefers SOC 2 + limited on-site/remote assessment rather than broad "audit rights" language.
- For penetration testing, we need the proposed window and whether Redwood requires a scoping call / NDA before access. We typically expect a 2-week window and a single annual pen-test.
- Evidence delivery: what SLA can Redwood commit to for providing artifact requests (logs, configurations, SOC 2 reports)? Procurement needs an expected turnaround to plan their audit.

If you can share a redline or a short note on cadence and scope by EOD that would help.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Shah
Security Lead, Atlas Health
attachments: none

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@atlashealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-03T09:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Audit rights / evidence cadence and pen-test window

Samir —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick summary from our side and attached drafts: "redlined-security-exhibit_v2.pdf" and an evidence index. Key points we propose for the Order Form / exhibit:

- Scope: limit audit rights to (a) review of Redwood's SOC 2 report(s) covering the in-scope services, (b) remote access for evidence review, and (c) one mutually-scheduled penetration test per 12 months. We do not accept open-ended on-site audits without prior agreement.
- Notice & scheduling: 30 days' notice for requests that require engineering time; SOC 2 evidence requests: Redwood will triage and respond within 10 business days for standard artifacts, 20 business days for deeper operational evidence (config dumps, longer logs).
- Pen-test requirements: signed pen-test NDA + scoping call 10 business days before test start, limited to pre-production/staging environment and production read-only endpoints where necessary. All testing must conform to an agreed scope (IP ranges, assets, and test cases).
- Data handling: any evidence that contains customer data will be redacted or provided via secure share; we can provide investigator-level logs but not raw storage snapshots without a court order.

Next steps I'd suggest: Laura (legal) can confirm whether those timelines are acceptable from a contract-risk perspective; Marcus (security ops) will map the staging window options. I attached an evidence-index spreadsheet to show typical artifacts and sample turnaround times.

Action items:
- Laura: review redlines in attached PDF and suggest alternative language where needed.
- Marcus: propose two candidate pen-test windows in April/May.
- Samir: if procurement has a preferred SLA, flag it here and we'll try to align.

Best,
Priyom Das
Dir, Solutions — Redwood Inference
attachments: redlined-security-exhibit_v2.pdf, evidence-index.xlsx

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Samir Shah <samir.shah@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Audit rights / evidence cadence and pen-test window

Thanks Priyom — I reviewed the draft and made a few protective redlines (see attached "msa-excerpt-redlines.docx"). High-level legal notes:

- Narrow the audit clause: prefer language that references "SOC 2 Type II reports and related attestation materials" and allows a single remote audit per 12-month period that is limited to systems used to provide the in-scope services. Avoid broad "inspect any records" phrasing.
- Evidence turnaround: we can agree to 10 business days for commonly-requested artifacts (SOC 2 reports, summary logs, configuration excerpts). For ad-hoc requests that require engineering time (e.g., extended full-log exports, packet captures), propose 20 business days and a capped number of such requests per year (suggest 6).
- Pen-test: require a mutual NDA and scoping call; allow pen-tests on non-prod by default and on production only under strict guardrails (read-only tests, pre-approved test cases, controlled blast radius). We should require that the customer use a third-party pen-test vendor approved by Redwood and provide proof of insurance.
- Evidence retention: call out that Redwood retains certain operational logs for a baseline period (30–90 days depending on type) and that longer-retention requests will be treated as professional services.

I've added inline alternatives that protect Redwood's IP and operational stability while giving Atlas the artifacts they typically need. We should push for the SOC 2 attestation + limited remote review as the primary audit mechanism and keep on-site access as an exception requiring escalation.

I'll add suggested contract language in the MSA excerpt and run it by legal. Marcus, can you confirm staging availability and typical turnaround for providing sanitized logs?

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: msa-excerpt-redlines.docx

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T13:18:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Audit rights / evidence cadence and pen-test window

Laura / Priyom / Samir —

Operational notes from security ops:

- Pen-test windows: we can offer two candidate 5-business-day windows in May (May 10–14; May 24–28). Each window requires the NDA signed + scoping call at least 10 business days prior. We can support one full vendor test per year; additional tests can be scheduled but may require extra fees and capacity approval.
- Evidence turnaround: for the artifacts listed in the evidence-index, we can target 7–10 business days for typical items (SOC 2 report, access logs snippets, configuration exports). For anything that requires longer forensic extraction we need 15–20 business days.
- Delivery method: secure SFTP or an encrypted Drive link; we will redact PII and provide sanitized exports where feasible. If Atlas requires raw snapshots we need a written legal request and additional approvals.

Samir — let me know which May window you prefer and the vendor details. We'll block the calendar tentatively after the NDA/scoping call.

Marcus Lin
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is helpful and aligns with what procurement needs. Quick answers:

- Procurement is comfortable with SOC 2 Type II + a single remote inspection per year as the primary mechanism. They want the 10 business day SLA for standard artifacts documented in the Order Form.
- For pen-test, May 24–28 works best for our vendor (Veridian Security). We'll share vendor contact and insurance proof by Monday. We accept the NDA + scoping call requirement.
- A few small asks: can Redwood include the 10-business-day evidence SLA in the Order Form (so it's enforceable for the PO) and confirm the maximum number of ad-hoc deep artifact requests per year (we can accept the proposed cap of 6).

If you can push a final redline that incorporates Laura's language and the two points above, procurement will route for signature.

Best,
